newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Bosnia war invalid plans North Pole parachute jump.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia war invalid plans North Pole parachute jump.

text.p: A Bosnian Serb who lost most of his right leg during the Bosnian war plans a parachute jump over the North Pole to encourage other war invalids, the official Tanjug news agency said on Thursday.
Miodrag Hrnjez began jumping last year when he met the captain of the Yugoslav national parachuting team who had formed a club called "Sky Open to All" to help first category invalids learn to jump.

"I began practicing first by jumping off a crate, then off a bed, and on October 4 last year I jumped for the first time from a helicopter from a height of 2,100 metres (6,500 feet) onto a beach (in Montenegro)," Hrnjez was quoted as saying.

Wounds on Hrnjez' left leg have not healed completely but despite doctors' fears he would remain in a wheelchair, he is now walking again. "With my forthcoming jump over the North Pole, I want to encourage all war invalids to continue fighting for their recovery," Hrnjez said.
Details of when the jump would happen were not available.
